correctness.rationale: The four spectral projectors follow from symmetric BIBD incidence identities; direct Schur-square expansion gives the two stated blocks. Singular-value decomposition on zero-mean subspaces gives eigenvalues \(1,0,c+d,c-d\) with all multiplicities. The inequality \(|v-2k|\le v-4\) and \(s\ge1\) establishes \(c-d\ge1/v>0\) for all \(2\le k\le v-2\). At \(k=v-1\) a missing-incidence permutation gives a \(v\)-dimensional kernel. The converse characterization follows from \(BB^{\mathsf T}=s^2 I+(k^2-s^2)J/v\). Five exact rational finite constructions with \(v\in\{3,4,7,11,13\}\) checked the matrix formula, annihilating polynomial and ranks; no finite-to-infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The class comprises all connected regular bipartite graphs with four adjacency energy levels, and includes projective-plane incidence graphs regardless of planarity/automorphisms. A complete spectrum and probability table with all multiplicities, a rank dichotomy, exact kernel, design-independent trace and positive spectral gap is an intrinsically motivated quantum-transport classification. It is not a finite census, arbitrary numerical slice, or restatement of the ordinary adjacency spectrum.
